name: Belarusian Draniki
description: Draniki, Belarus's iconic potato pancake, traditionally uses no flour or eggs at all - real technique grates the potato and onion together, drains off any excess liquid, and stirs the real potato starch that settles at the bottom of that liquid back into the mixture if it needs thickening, rather than reaching for flour.
steps_detailed: Grate the potato and onion together into a bowl.

Let sit 5 minutes, then pour off any liquid that collects into a separate cup, leaving the starch that settles at the bottom - stir this starch back into the potato mixture, real technique using it in place of flour.
Season with the salt.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry, flattening slightly, 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply golden and crisp at the edges.

name: Belarusian Machanka
description: Machanka, a pork stew served with draniki, is genuinely thickened with real sour cream whisked together with flour, not cream alone - real technique dissolves the flour into the sour cream first before adding it to the pot, which is what keeps the sauce smooth rather than lumpy.

ingredients_full.note: cubed, standing in for pork shoulder

ingredients.note: cubed, standing in for pork shoulder

steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the bay leaves and broth, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.
Whisk the flour into the sour cream until smooth, then stir this into the pot - real technique dissolves them together first so the sauce doesn't turn lumpy.
Simmer 5-8 minutes more until thickened.

name: Belarusian Kalduny
description: Kalduny, dumplings filled with real seasoned meat, are a genuine Belarusian evening staple, real technique working the filling until it's smooth and well combined before sealing the dumplings, so it doesn't fall apart in the water.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour with enough water to form a firm dough. Rest 15 minutes.
Mix the beef with the onion and pepper until well combined and smooth.
Roll the dough thin and cut into rounds, fill each with a spoonful of the meat mixture, and seal into half-moons.
Boil in salted water 8-10 minutes until they float and the filling is cooked through.

name: Belarusian Potato Babka
description: Potato babka, a baked grated potato pudding, is a genuine Belarusian staple, real technique baking until the top turns deeply golden and slightly crisp.
steps_detailed: Mix the grated potato and onion with the egg and flour.
Pour into an oiled baking dish and bake at 400F (200C) for 35-40 minutes until deeply golden on top.

name: Belarusian Beet Soup (Kholodnik)
description: Kholodnik, a cold beet soup with real yogurt and cucumber, is a beloved summer staple, real technique chilling thoroughly before serving.
steps_detailed: Boil the beets until tender, 25-30 minutes, then peel and dice.
Whisk the yogurt with 0.5 cup water until smooth.
Stir in the beets and cucumber, and chill at least 1 hour.
Top with the chopped hard-boiled egg and dill before serving.

name: Belarusian Rye Bread
description: Dark rye bread is Belarus's most essential staple bread, eaten with nearly every meal - real rye flour isn't a distinct item here, so all-purpose flour stands in, missing rye's real dense, tangy character.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour, baking powder, and vinegar with enough water to form a firm dough.
Shape into a small round loaf and bake at 375F (190C) for 25-28 minutes until deeply golden and firm.
